title: Workspace Pod Navigator — dynamic route scoping and progressive rail disclosure
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Goal: Redesign the console navigation to better support rapid switching between multiple workspaces and surface task-relevant rails without overwhelming users. Current sidebar patterns conflate global navigation and per-workspace task flows; this ticket explores a split approach: a persistent global primary rail (left) for top-level areas (Models, Deployments, Usage, Billing) and a second ephemeral ‘pod’ rail scoped to the active workspace that reveals contextual routes and micro-hubs (dashboards, rollout controls, cost breakdowns).

Background: Engineering metrics show frequent context switches across 2–6 workspaces per session for platform teams. Usability tests indicate users lose orientation when the left rail reorders significantly after switching. We need a pattern that preserves global orientation, speeds workspace-scoped navigation, and keeps route history discoverable.

Proposed solution: "Pod Navigator" concept — a compact workspace chip in the top-left that expands the ephemeral pod rail when clicked or on hotkey. Key behaviors: persistent global rail stays visible at all times; pod rail slides in with workspace-scoped routes and quick actions; pod rail supports pinning of up to 3 micro-hubs (e.g., Rollouts, Cost View, Traces) and a ‘recent routes’ strip; transition animations emphasize route continuity (micro-crumbs flash on route change). Accessibility: keyboard nav and focus trap for the pod, ARIA labels for pinned micro-hubs.

UX decisions and trade-offs: we prioritize fast switching and discoverability over maximum immediate visibility. This means the pod rail is collapsed by default on narrow screens to preserve content width. Batching of micro-hub cards reduces cognitive load but adds one more tap to reach deep settings — acceptable for power users who can pin hubs.

Metrics for success: reduced average time-to-route after workspace switch by >= 25%, fewer lost-orientation incidents in moderated tests, and 15% increased usage of workspace-specific dashboards within 2 weeks of rollout.

Implementation notes: Deliver high-fidelity Figma prototype + interactive InVision microflow. Coordinate with ENG on stable left-rail IDs to avoid breaking deep links. Provide a migration spec for existing user-customized sidebar order.
